claim: CAS namespace files are keyed by an opaque `NamespaceLifeId`, so debris from one namespace life cannot be addressed through a later life with the same namespace name.
The namespace-file key shape is `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_files/<relative-name>`.
A reader or `CaInlineWriteBuffer` retains the exact `NamespaceLifeId` selected at operation start and does not re-resolve the namespace name during that operation.
Fresh namespace-file resolution accepts only a `Live` catalog life and rejects `Creating`, `Removing`, or absent catalog rows without durable mutation.
Steady-state namespace-file operations do not issue hot-path requests for catalog, ref-blob, manifest, or blob keys.
A reader holding a life from before same-name rebirth can return only the old life's bytes or absence; it must never return successor-life bytes.
Delayed inline finalization cannot change the successor life's token or bytes; it writes only under the captured old life or fails with a typed stale-write exception.

Physical `_files` debris is outside namespace rebirth gating; incomplete `LIST` may defer reclamation and leak bytes, but cannot expose an old file through a new life or prevent the new life from being admitted.
The perpetual dead-life janitor owns namespace-life debris, while the orphan-manifest sweep owns orphan manifest bytes; both are cleanup mechanisms rather than identity or rebirth gates.

The generation-6 opaque-life layout cut and generation-7 unified ref-life wire cut are recreate-only format boundaries with no compatibility parser, copy-forward path, or fallback that reinterprets older name-keyed objects as current life-keyed files.

`ContentAddressedTransaction::writeFile` classifies table-level files through `parseTableFilePath` and writes them with `putNamespaceFile`; other paths use a server-root-qualified `putMountpointObject` key.
Loose mountpoint objects use `roots/<server_root_id>/<path>` and carry no namespace, catalog row, life id, or later namespace-name resolution, so same-name namespace rebirth cannot retarget them.

An unresolved every-attempt writer grant may correspond to a durable precommit; failure queues an in-memory cleanup duty while the mount lives, `Adopted` resolution requires exact owner removal before retirement, and `Rejected` resolution proves that no owner exists.

`INV_NO_RETIRE_UNCERTAIN_GRANT` prevents a writer cleanup duty from disappearing while the grant outcome is unknown; successor cleanup remains the seal-derived path for durable precommits left by a dead predecessor.
Exact GET and decode nominate an orphan manifest as a neutral candidate without consuming a B2 ordinal or entering unmatched-remove accounting.
`CommitRound` adopts an orphan nomination in the round's `gc/state` CAS, and only an adopted nomination may reach exact-token manifest deletion.

If a process dies after orphan-nomination adoption and before manifest deletion, the manifest remains leak-safe and rediscoverable; the protocol does not promise that the dead process retries deletion.

The branch reconstruction goal is to build only upstream fixes, the CAS subsystem, its integration, tests, CI wiring, and user-facing documentation as a readable grouped commit series on top of `altinity/antalya-26.6`.

The carve script does not promise per-commit buildability, hunk-level splitting of mixed files, history rewriting or preservation, pushing, pull-request creation, or building; only the reconstructed tip must equal the source tree minus excluded paths.
The carve interface is `utils/cas-carve/carve.sh [--src <ref>] [--base <ref>] [--branch <name>] [--check] [--force]`, defaulting to `HEAD`, `altinity/antalya-26.6`, and `cas-carved`.

The carve classifier processes EXCLUDES before ordered GROUPS, uses first-match-wins classification, hard-fails with the complete unmatched-file list, and warns rather than failing when a group matches zero files.

The carve apply phase creates a temporary worktree at `tmp/carve-worktree` from `git merge-base $BASE $SRC`, checks out or removes each classified source file in manifest order, and commits each non-empty group with its group message.

The carve completeness invariant requires `git diff <branch>..$SRC --name-only` restricted by the exclude pathspecs to be empty; the script prints unrestricted differences as the discarded report summarized by exclude category.
The carve manifest excludes `docs/superpowers/`, `.superpowers/`, `utils/ca-soak/`, `utils/cas-gate/`, `utils/cas-carve/`, `tmp/`, `.gitignore`, and `tests/broken_tests.yaml`.

Within `tests/queries/0_stateless/`, added files belong to the new CAS stateless-test group and modified files belong to the old-test-tag group; this requires `--name-status` plus `added-only` and `modified-only` path matching.
CAS subsystem commits are ordered bottom-up as `Primitives` → `Formats` → `Backend` → `Pool` → `Parts` → `Gc` → `Tools` → `benchmarks`, followed by integration, tests, CI/tags, and documentation.

Files under `docs/superpowers/`, `.superpowers/`, `utils/ca-soak/`, `utils/cas-gate/`, `utils/cas-carve/`, `tmp/`, `.claude/`, `.gitignore`, and `tests/broken_tests.yaml` are deliberately excluded from the carved branch as worklogs, model/report artifacts, gate infrastructure, agent tooling, artifacts, or test metadata.

Before each carve regeneration, run `utils/cas-carve/carve.sh --check`; if the base advances, merge it into the working branch, let the merge-base move, and remove groups reported as empty when their fixes were absorbed upstream.

The carve classifier cannot distinguish junk files placed inside an included directory glob, so hygiene of included source directories remains a review concern; file moves may change which grouped commit carries a file without changing the feature tip.

The planned Bash matcher uses plain `[[ <repo-relative-path> == <glob> ]]` semantics where `*` crosses `/`; an optional `A:` or `M:` prefix restricts a pattern to files added or modified relative to the merge-base.

The carve script must hard-fail on an unmatched diff file, a completeness-invariant violation, or an existing target branch without `--force`; an empty group is warning-only, and the script must not use sleep-style waiting or push.
The S3 conditional-write policy treats HTTP 412 as deterministic and non-retryable, exposed through `S3Exception::isPreconditionFailed` and `RetryStrategy`.

The B115 `ReadBufferFromFileView` fix recomputes its offset from the inner buffer after every right-bound change because `ReadBufferFromS3` resets its working buffer; the same change includes `ReadBufferFromMemory` coverage.
The B117 fix stops `ReadBufferFromS3`'s outer retry loop after `KILL QUERY` by checking `CurrentThread::get().isQueryCanceled()`.
The B90 `ThreadGroup` fix makes a borrowed child retain a `shared_ptr` to its parent group so background work cannot use freed parent counters.

The B37 `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog` fix throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when `current_writer` is absent instead of relying on a release-build `chassert` no-op; a missing `logs_dir` remains normal for storages that do not materialize empty directories.

Conditional S3 PUT/COPY operations use `If-Match` and `If-None-Match`, while GCS uses `x-goog-if-generation-match` with native GOOG4 signing because AWS SigV4 `If-Match` semantics are insufficient for GCS.

The disk-transaction integration makes one logical part use one transaction, makes in-flight resolve read-your-writes state, and keeps projection sub-parts from committing before the parent whole-part transaction.

The carve stateless-test group matches only added files under `tests/queries/`, while the CI/tag group matches only modified files under that tree; this prevents new tests and old-test tag edits from sharing a commit.
The planned apply phase uses `git worktree add -b $BRANCH $WT $MB`, commits each group with `git commit -F -`, and removes the temporary worktree on exit while retaining the branch.

The planned completeness check compares `git diff --name-only --no-renames HEAD $SRC_SHA`, counts only paths matching EXCLUDES as discarded, and reports every non-excluded difference as a lost file before failing.
